replication.verdict: Bill's since-2016 numbers are not replicated on daily bars. He quotes 19.5% a year since 2016 against SPY at 15.4%, with a worst drop of -45% against SPY's -34%, and 17.0% against 11.5% since 2022. He also quotes 72% winning boosts, about 8 a year, about 3 days each, and a standalone 3x version around 11-12% a year. On these prices, since 2016, the next-open fill compounds at 16.2% against close-to-close SPY at 14.6%, max drawdown -35.9% against -33.7%. The close fill, the optimistic stand-in for a 12:50 PT trade, compounds at 17.1% with max drawdown -35.9%. Since 2022 the next-open fill is 12.9% against SPY 11.5%, and the close fill is 14.7% against SPY 11.5%. From 2006 the next-open fill is 12.4% (max drawdown -55.1%, worst year 2008 -36.8%) and the close fill is 12.7%. Next-open boosts since 2016: win rate 77.4% (75.3% beat SPY), 8.6 a year, 3.3 days on average, average P&L 0.8%, worst -7.4%. Close-fill boosts: win rate 74.2%, 8.6 a year, 3.3 days. Standalone UPRO-or-cash since 2016 is 10.4% next-open and 14.5% at the close. The deflated Sharpe of the next-open book's daily gap over SPY, on the 2006-onward window and the full ledger, is 0.311. Over the lead book it is 0.000. Removing 2012, the year the gap over SPY added the most, leaves a strategy compound growth of 11.8% against SPY 10.8%. The walk-forward pick on the next-open grid is rsi15_f50_n10; the published signal stays the named rule. The gap versus his quote is the 12:50 PT price versus a daily close, the fill (this close versus the next open), UPRO's financing and expense ratio in the stitched series, 5 bps per side, and the rule that an exit close does not re-enter.

caveats: Leveraged ETFs before the listing are a daily-reset model: leverage times the underlying, minus financing at the lagged T-bill plus 0.40%, minus the assumed expense ratio. Listed returns replace the model after the first real close-to-close bar. UGL is 2x gold. TMF is 3x TLT. Expense ratios are assumptions (TMF 1.03%, UGL 0.95%), not a prospectus scrape.
Cash is the lagged 13-week bill yield, not the BIL NAV. The signal names that residual BIL.
The exposure rows are fixed rules on the 2006-onward window. They are not a walk-forward selection. The 2.0x row is the live book and is not a new trial. The other rows are.
Mean-reversion entries sit on one ordered list so the materiality bar has neighbors. RSI 5/10/15 is a real step. IBS and the 5-day band are different rules on that list, not a smooth scale.
Deflated Sharpe uses every counting trial in the ledger, including this run. A high full-sample Sharpe can still have a low deflated Sharpe.
The 50/50 blend rebalances every session. That is a research combination, not a cheaper trading rule.
Bitcoin at 5 bps per side is cheaper than a retail coin fill. The 28 bp audit is the repo's Coinbase-like preset and is not a selection trial.

Bill's RSI boost is checked on daily bars. A fill at the signal close is an optimistic stand-in for a 12:50 PT trade. The next open is the conservative fill, and it is the one the signal file uses. Neither fill is the intraday price he sees at 12:50.
The published RSI boost is the named rule (RSI below 10, one third into UPRO, 10-session cap), not the walk-forward pick. The grid is in the ledger so the deflated Sharpe counts those looks.
This is research on public prices. It is not a recommendation to buy leveraged ETFs.
